Short Description (Text): Shanghai Metro opened in 1993 with construction starting in 1986. The system became the world's largest metro by route length serving multiple districts.
Major metro system expansion occurred between 2003 and 2010 leading up to the World Expo. The system grew rapidly during this period adding multiple new lines.
NDRC approved the 2018-2023 construction planning including nine new lines. The plan aimed for 27 metro lines covering 1154 kilometers after completion.
Development of high-speed rail connections linking Shanghai to regional and national destinations. Airport and railway station integration expanded.
New traffic planning guidelines issued to expand bike lane networks across all districts. Instructions provided for safe passages and infrastructure for cyclists.
Construction of a 25km bike and walkway trail on the Pudong side of the Huangpu River providing dedicated cycling infrastructure.

Measure (Label): Alternative Drive Systems and Sharing Offers
Short Description (Text): Shanghai participated in national pilot program providing incentives for new energy vehicles including subsidies and free license plates for electric vehicles.

Measure (Label): Alternative Drive Systems and Sharing Offers
Short Description (Text): Mandate requiring all new or updated buses and cruising cabs to use NEVs. Public sector vehicles prioritized for electrification.

Measure (Label): Alternative Drive Systems and Sharing Offers
Short Description (Text): Government set targets for 6000 service spots and 20000 NEVs for car-sharing by 2020. Free parking and subsidies provided to operators.

Measure (Label): Alternative Drive Systems and Sharing Offers
Short Description (Text): Jiading district provided subsidies of approximately 5180 euros per NEV per year for car-sharing services to encourage electric vehicle adoption.

Measure (Label): Alternative Drive Systems and Sharing Offers
Short Description (Text): Shanghai stopped offering free license plates for plug-in hybrids starting 2023 to support development of pure electric vehicles.
All metro stations provided with 5G network coverage enabling smart transportation management and passenger information systems.
City-level energy monitoring platform established to track public building consumption. System expanded for continuous data collection.
Changning District retrofitted 32 public buildings achieving average 20% energy savings. Monitoring platform tracked 160 of 165 public buildings.
Government subsidy program providing 40 yuan per square meter for projects reducing energy consumption by more than 20% using Energy Performance Contracting.
Mandatory building energy efficiency standards implemented requiring new buildings to meet energy performance requirements and include renewable energy systems.
Urban green space development as carbon sinks. By 2010 urban green spaces accounted for portion of total land area with vegetation carbon storage capacity.
Shanghai Green Belt forest planting program over 20 years. Monoculture and mixed forests planted for carbon sequestration with monitoring and research.
Chongming Island developed as carbon-neutral demonstration zone with high forest coverage serving as urban forest carbon sink research station.
Shanghai set targets for nearly zero energy buildings achieving 206% completion rate by 2022. Local government provided 3% floor area bonus as incentive.

Measure (Label): Sustainable Land Management (Avoidance of Urban Sprawl)
Short Description (Text): Ecological civilization policy mandated percentages of urban parks trees green roofs and vertical gardens to manage urban expansion and preserve carbon stocks.

Bus rapid transit system with 22 stations covering 21 km from Surjani Town to Numaish Chowrangi with dedicated bus corridors and 80 diesel hybrid buses to reduce traffic congestion and improve public transport access.

Action_Name: Orange Line BRT Abdul Sattar Edhi Line
Short Description (Text): Operational BRT line connecting various districts to integrate with Green Line BRT and expand public transport network in the city.
Planned 27 km BRT corridor from Numaish Chowrangi to Malir Halt via University Road with biomethane fuel system supported by UN Green Climate Fund for emissions reduction.
Development of ITS-based traffic management model for metropolitan areas with Karachi as pilot study conducted by University of Mississippi and NED University.
Electronic challan system using cameras at intersections to automatically detect traffic violations and issue digital fines to improve traffic law enforcement and reduce corruption.
Pedestrianized street near Denso Hall Library in Old Town Karachi developed with terracotta tiles by Heritage Foundation of Pakistan to improve walkability.

Development and notification of Pakistan Green Building Code 2023 led by NED University Karachi and Pakistan Engineering Council to promote energy-efficient construction and reduce building emissions.
Planned eco-friendly infrastructure with solar power implementation in residential development to promote sustainable green communities.

Measure (Label): Sustainable Land Management (Avoidance of Urban Sprawl)
Short Description (Text): Strategic development plan approved to guide coordinated urban growth and prevent uncontrolled sprawl with legal status under Sindh Local Government Ordinance 2001.
